What crystal system and space group does the crystalline adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework adopt?
It adopts the triclinic crystal system and the P-1 space group.

What principal metal, porphyrin, adenine, oxido, and water components are present in the asymmetric unit of the crystalline adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework, and where do three zinc ions reside?

The asymmetric unit contains nine Zn2+ ions, three meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin ligands, two adenine ligands, two bridging oxido ligands, and two coordinated water molecules; three zinc ions occupy the vacant porphyrin sites.
In the final framework of the adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin material, how are the paddlewheel Zn clusters assembled, and what channel type is present?

Adenine connects dinuclear zinc-carboxylate paddlewheel clusters into a hexanuclear zinc cluster, which is decorated by twelve meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin ligands; the final framework leaves 1D rhombus-shaped channels.
What internal-surface structural feature of the anionic adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework is proposed to influence dye adsorption?

Open Watson-Crick faces constructed by adenine and the meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin linker periodically decorate the channel interior; together with uncoordinated carboxylate oxygen sites, they may provide adsorption ability toward specific dye molecules.
What solvent-accessible volume and porosity are calculated for the final framework of the adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin material?
A PLATON calculation gives an accessible volume of approximately 75%, corresponding to 15858.2 Å3 within a cell volume of 21050.7 Å3.
What thermal-stability behavior does the synthesized adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework exhibit?
It exhibits high thermal stability, attributed to the introduction of auxiliary nitrogen-containing ligands.
What N2 uptake and BET/Langmuir surface areas does the activated adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework show at 77 K?
The activated framework adsorbs 286 cm3 g-1 N2 at 77 K, with calculated BET and Langmuir surface areas of 622.8 and 918.5 m2 g-1, respectively.
In the dye-adsorption tests, which dyes are taken up by the anionic adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework, and what mechanism is proposed for the uptake?

It adsorbs cationic methylene blue (MB+) but does not adsorb neutral red (NR0) or anionic methyl orange (MO−), even though NR0 and MO− are size-accessible. The MB+ uptake is attributed to ion exchange with dimethylammonium counterions in the anionic framework.

After 5 h of dye adsorption, what percentages of methylene blue (MB+), basic violet 14 (BV14+), and rhodamine 6G (R6G+) are absorbed by the solid adenine-containing zinc-porphyrin framework, and what size-related behavior is proposed?

It absorbs 92% of MB+, 75.8% of BV14+, and 59.5% of R6G+. The differences are attributed to a dye-size effect: the smaller MB+ molecules enter the pores more easily than the larger BV14+ and R6G+ molecules.
What crystal system and asymmetric-unit composition does the 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework have?

It crystallizes in the triclinic P-1 space group, with an asymmetric unit containing 6.5 Zn2+ ions, 1.5 meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin ligands, six 1H-1,2,3-triazole-derived ligands, and six coordinated water molecules.
What pentanuclear zinc cluster, channel structure, and solvent-accessible volume are present in the 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework?

The framework contains a pentanuclear zinc cluster in which a central zinc ion, coordinated by six 1H-1,2,3-triazole-derived ligands, connects four additional zinc ions through those ligands; six meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin ligands decorate this cluster, producing a 3D framework with 1D rhombus-shaped channels along the c axis. A PLATON calculation gives an accessible volume of about 65%, corresponding to 6286.1 Å3 in 9647.0 Å3.
What porphyrin-linker vacancies and carboxylate binding modes are present in the 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework?
Two additional zinc ions occupy the vacant porphyrin sites; the meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin carboxylate groups bind four Zn2+ ions through either chelating or monodentate modes.
What N2 adsorption capacity and surface areas does the activated 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework exhibit at 77 K?
The activated framework adsorbs 200 cm3 g-1 N2 at 77 K, with calculated BET and Langmuir surface areas of 456.1 and 678.2 m2 g-1, respectively; its type-I N2 isotherms indicate microporosity.
What charge-selective dye adsorption behavior and proposed mechanism does the anionic 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework show?

It adsorbs cationic methylene blue (MB+) but does not adsorb neutral red (NR0) or anionic methyl orange (MO−), although NR0 and MO− are size-accessible. The uptake is attributed to ion exchange with dimethylammonium counterions in the anionic framework.

After 5 h of dye adsorption, what percentages of methylene blue (MB+), basic violet 14 (BV14+), and rhodamine 6G (R6G+) are absorbed by the solid 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework, and what size-related behavior is proposed?

It absorbs 91.3% of MB+, 70.8% of BV14+, and 50% of R6G+. The differences are attributed to a dye-size effect: the smaller MB+ molecules enter the pores more easily than the larger BV14+ and R6G+ molecules.
What thermal-stability behavior does the synthesized 1H-1,2,3-triazole-containing zinc-porphyrin framework exhibit?
It exhibits high thermal stability, attributed to the introduction of auxiliary nitrogen-containing ligands.

In the crystalline cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate, which donor atoms bind each Co(II) center, and what coordination environment does this produce?

Each Co(II) center is coordinated by two monodentate carboxylate oxygen atoms from two 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate ligands, two nitrogen atoms from the azopyridine linker, and two oxygen atoms from coordinated water, giving a distorted octahedral O4N2 coordination environment.

In the crystalline cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate, what Co-O and Co-N bond distances are measured, and what type of framework do these ligands generate around cobalt?
The Co-O bond distances are 2.124 to 2.141 Å, the Co-N distance is 2.218 Å, and the ligands linked through Co(II) form a finite 2D framework along the c-axis.

What interactions extend the layered network of the cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate, and what effect do these interactions have on the material?

The layered network is extended by intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonds with distances of 2.789 Å and 2.883 Å, respectively, and by layer-by-layer pi-pi stacking; these interactions improve network strength and stability and contribute to the framework's electrochemical performance.

In what lattice system does the crystalline cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate crystallize, and what components are present in its asymmetric unit?

It crystallizes in a triclinic lattice system; its asymmetric unit contains one Co(II) ion, half of a 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate ligand, half of an azopyridine linker, and two coordinated water molecules.
What do powder X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy indicate about the synthesized cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate?

The powder X-ray diffraction pattern matches the pattern simulated from single-crystal X-ray diffraction data for the framework, confirming structural phase purity, and scanning electron microscopy shows rod-like morphologies.

Under nitrogen thermogravimetric analysis from 50 to 800 °C at 10 °C min^-1, what thermal behavior does the cobalt(II) framework containing coordinated water, 4,4'-azopyridine, and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate exhibit, and what is assigned to the initial weight loss?

It shows a minimal initial weight loss between 35 °C and 198 °C, attributed to elimination of water molecules, and remains thermally stable up to 350 °C; subsequent weight loss corresponds to decomposition of the organic framework.

What are the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area and Barrett-Joyner-Halenda average pore diameter of the cobalt(II) mixed-ligand framework measured by N2 adsorption at 77 K, and how are these pore properties linked to electrochemical function?

The framework has a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 23.3 m^2 g^-1 and a Barrett-Joyner-Halenda average pore diameter of 1.69 nm; these pores facilitate ion diffusion throughout the material, allowing use of electroactive sites and supporting charge storage.

What do X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy measurements indicate about the cobalt oxidation state and fluorination of the cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate, and what pseudocapacitive role does Co(II) play?

X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that cobalt is predominantly in the +2 oxidation state and that an F 1s peak at 687.48 eV confirms C-F bonds and fluorination of the framework; the Co(II) centers contribute pseudocapacitive behavior through reversible Co(II)/Co(III) redox reactions.
In a three-electrode configuration using 2 M KOH electrolyte, what does cyclic voltammetry of the cobalt(II) mixed-ligand framework reveal about its charge-storage mechanism and rate capability?

As the scan rate increases, the cyclic voltammograms retain their shape while the enclosed area increases proportionally, indicating excellent rate capability and electrochemical stability; the two well-defined redox peaks show pseudocapacitive charge storage arising from intercalation and deintercalation of OH- ions during faradaic redox processes.

Under three-electrode measurements with 2 M KOH electrolyte, what specific capacitance does the cobalt(II) mixed-ligand framework achieve at 1 A g^-1, and why does its specific capacitance decrease at higher current densities?

It achieves a specific capacitance of 956 F g^-1 at 1 A g^-1; at higher current densities, the shorter charge-discharge time limits electrolyte-ion access to the inner porous structure, causing incomplete utilization of active ionic species and decreasing the capacitance.

What structural and fluorination-related mechanisms explain the high electrochemical capacitance of the cobalt(II) framework formed from 4,4'-azopyridine and 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzene-1,4-dicarboxylate?

The layered framework has van der Waals interactions, pi-pi stacking, and hydrogen bonding, which enlarge the interlayer space; fluorine functionalization reduces electron density around Co(II), facilitates Co(II)/Co(III) redox transitions, increases electrochemically active sites, promotes pseudocapacitive behavior, and provides fluorine atoms that act as an effective charge-host framework, strengthening intermolecular interactions and improving electronic conductivity.
What cycling retention does the cobalt(II) mixed-ligand framework show after 9000 galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles at 15 A g^-1 in a three-electrode configuration?
It retains 82% of its capacitance after 9000 galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles at 15 A g^-1.
What crystal system and space group does the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer adopt?
It adopts an orthorhombic crystal system with space group Pbcn.
What Cu4I4 cluster geometry is present in the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer?
The Cu4I4 clusters in the framework have a U-shaped geometry.

What dimensionality and network topology do the Cu4I4 clusters and N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide ligands create in the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer?
Deformed Cu4I4 clusters are linked by the ligand into a two-dimensional (4,4) network.
How are the layers in the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer stacked and linked by hydrogen bonds?
The two-dimensional layers stack in an ABAB arrangement and are connected by N-H...O hydrogen bonds, with an N...O distance of 2.943(2) Å and an N-H...O angle of 167.8(6)°.

How is the disordered solvent electron density in the crystal structure of the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer treated, and what guest molecules is it tentatively assigned to?

No satisfactory disorder model could be built for the solvent; PLATON/SQUEEZE was used to remove the residual electron density, which was tentatively assigned to one N,N-diethylformamide molecule and one-half acetonitrile molecule per formula unit.
What do powder X-ray diffraction measurements indicate about the phase purity and water stability of the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer?
Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the material is phase pure, and its framework remains stable in water for 24 h.
What thermal stability is shown by thermogravimetric analysis for the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer?
The framework is thermally stable up to about 320 °C.
What functional consequence is associated with the large free volume remaining after solvent removal from the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer?
The large remaining free volume provides potential space for mass transport.

Which metal ion most strongly quenches the luminescence of the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer, and what relative quenching order is observed for the tested metal ions in ethanol and water?

What Stern-Volmer quenching constants are obtained for Fe3+ quenching of the Cu4I4(N,N'-bis(pyridin-3-yl)cyclohexane-1,4-dicarboxamide)2 coordination polymer, and over what Fe3+ concentration ranges were they derived?

What is the coordination framework dimensionality of the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer?

What carboxylate coordination mode gives the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer a one-dimensional chain-like framework?

Each truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate linker coordinates through only two carboxylate groups in chelating bidentate modes, while the other two carboxylate groups remain uncoordinated. This reduced connectivity gives one-dimensional chains.

What is the shortest distance between adjacent sulfur atoms in the crystal structure of the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer?

What solid-state cyclic voltammetric redox processes are observed for the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer at a scan rate of 100 mV s-1 in 0.1 M LiBF4/CH3CN, and how are they assigned?

What room-temperature electrical conductivity is obtained for pelletized samples of the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer?

What solid-state electron paramagnetic resonance signal is observed for the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer, and how is its rhombic anisotropy assigned?

What product of molar magnetic susceptibility and temperature (χ_M T) at 300 K in a 1 kOe DC field indicates a magnetic contribution from radical electrons in the cadmium(II) truncated tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate coordination polymer?
χ_M T is 0.155 cm^3 K mol^-1.

For the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate), what is its chemical identity and overall dimensionality of its Pb-S framework determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction?

What Pb coordination environment was revealed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction for the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate)?

What crystal-orientation and morphology observations link the plate surface and photoconductive pathway of the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate) to its 2D (-Pb-S-) sheets?

What thermal stability and decomposition behavior are observed for the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate) by TGA and DTA?

What chemical stability tests were performed on bulk samples of the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate), and what did they show?

What electronic band gap, orbital characters, and band-edge locations are predicted by first-principles calculations on the optimized structure of the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate)?

The spectrum shows a maximum absorption at 444 nm and an optical band gap of 2.50 eV.

For bulk samples of the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate), what absolute VBM and CBM levels were determined from photoelectron yield spectroscopy and optical band-gap data?

What fluorescence behavior is observed for the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate)?

What time-resolved microwave conductivity value was obtained for bulk powder of the lead 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate coordination polymer [Pb(tadt)]n (tadt = 1,3,4-thiadiazole-2,5-dithiolate), and what do the components represent?

What range of Co-O bond lengths is found for the two-dimensional cobalt(II) coordination polymer with empirical formula C45H40Co2N2O9?

What cobalt hydroxo unit is formed in the two-dimensional cobalt(II) coordination polymer with empirical formula C45H40Co2N2O9, and how is it linked to produce the framework?

What coordination connectivity does the deprotonated tricarboxylate ligand 4',4'',4'''-[nitrilotris(methylene)]tris(1,1'-biphenyl-2-carboxylate) have in the two-dimensional cobalt(II) coordination polymer with empirical formula C45H40Co2N2O9?

What cobalt(II) coordination geometry is observed in the cobalt coordination polymer with empirical formula C84H60Co3N2O12?

What IR evidence supports complete deprotonation of carboxylate groups in the cobalt coordination polymer with empirical formula C84H60Co3N2O12?

For the In(III) 5-(5-carboxylatopyridin-3-yl)benzene-1,3-dicarboxylate framework with dimethylammonium counterions, what crystal system and space group are assigned from single-crystal X-ray diffraction?

Does the pyridine nitrogen coordinate to the In(III) centers in the In(III) 5-(5-carboxylatopyridin-3-yl)benzene-1,3-dicarboxylate framework with dimethylammonium counterions?

Do the PXRD patterns of freshly prepared In(III) 5-(5-carboxylatopyridin-3-yl)benzene-1,3-dicarboxylate framework with dimethylammonium counterions indicate phase purity relative to its single-crystal structure?

What does PXRD show for the In(III) 5-(5-carboxylatopyridin-3-yl)benzene-1,3-dicarboxylate framework with dimethylammonium counterions after 24 h exposure to air or soaking in methanol?

What is the 1D channel diameter of the zinc 5-nitroisophthalate framework containing open-ring pyridyl dithienylethene ligands, and how is the nitro substituent oriented?

For the zinc 5-nitroisophthalate framework containing open-ring pyridyl dithienylethene ligands, why does the open-ring diarylethene ligand form support MOF formation while the corresponding closed-ring ligand form does not?

What is the Pb(II) coordination number, geometry, donor set, and Pb-N and Pb-O bond-length range in single-crystal [Pb(HOBTT)(H2O)2]n, where HOBTT denotes the 4,5-bis(1-hydroxytetrazol-5-yl)-2H-1,2,3-triazole-derived ligand?

How does HOBTT coordination determine the dimensionality of [Pb(HOBTT)(H2O)2]n, where HOBTT denotes the 4,5-bis(1-hydroxytetrazol-5-yl)-2H-1,2,3-triazole-derived ligand, and what interactions connect the resulting layers into a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture?

What supramolecular topology and degree of interpenetration result from the assembly of Zn(II) centers with deprotonated 4-carboxycinnamate and 1,3-bis(imidazol-1-ylmethyl)benzene ligands in the orthorhombic zinc(II) coordination polymer C24H20N4O4Zn?

In the single-crystal structure of the monoclinic hydrated cadmium(II) coordination polymer formed from deprotonated 4,4′-((1H-imidazole-1-yl)methylene)dibenzoate and 1,3-bis(imidazol-1-ylmethyl)benzene ligands, what is the coordination environment of the Cd(II) center that has three oxygen donors and three nitrogen donors, including distances to its imidazole nitrogen donors?

How do deprotonated 4,4′-((1H-imidazole-1-yl)methylene)dibenzoate and 1,3-bis(imidazol-1-ylmethyl)benzene ligands assemble the monoclinic hydrated cadmium(II) coordination polymer into its layered architecture?

During thermogravimetric analysis in N2 at 10°C min−1 from room temperature to 790°C, what initial mass loss is observed for the monoclinic hydrated cadmium(II) coordination polymer formed from deprotonated 4,4′-((1H-imidazole-1-yl)methylene)dibenzoate and 1,3-bis(imidazol-1-ylmethyl)benzene ligands, and how is it assigned?

What is the framework identity of the cadmium(II) host coordination polymer, and what crystal system and space group does it crystallize in?

What experimental evidence indicates that a fluoride ion occupies the center of the trinuclear cadmium cluster in the cadmium(II) host coordination polymer?

What is the asymmetric-unit composition and local cadmium coordination environment in the cadmium(II) host coordination polymer?

What three-dimensional network topology is formed by the cadmium(II) host coordination polymer?

What cage structure is present in the cadmium(II) host coordination polymer, and why is its triangular antiprism cage regarded as accessible to polyaromatic hydrocarbon guests?

What synthesis conditions and crystal appearance are associated with the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What crystallographic space group and asymmetric-unit composition characterize the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What coordination geometry and extended structural topology are described for the cadmium center in the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What solid-state visible-light absorption range and optical band gap are measured for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer, and what structural feature is associated with the visible absorption?

What semiconductor type and flat-band potential are determined for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

Which sacrificial electron donor gives the highest hydrogen-evolution activity for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer, and how do ethanol and triethanolamine compare?

Under optimized aqueous diethylamine visible-light conditions, what hydrogen evolution rate is measured for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What recycling and post-reaction characterization results support the stability of the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer during photocatalytic hydrogen evolution?

What photoelectrochemical photocurrent value and light-on/off behavior are observed for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What conduction-band and valence-band potentials are estimated for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer, and from which measurements are they derived?

What average time-resolved photoluminescence lifetime is measured for the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

How does the cadmium-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer achieve visible-light hydrogen evolution without additional photosensitizers or cocatalysts?

What crystallographic space group, asymmetric-unit composition, manganese coordination geometry, and network connectivity characterize the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What solid-state visible-light absorption range and optical band gap are measured for the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

What n-type semiconductor characteristics, flat-band potential, and band-edge positions are determined for the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer, and how are they associated with photocatalytic hydrogen evolution?

Under optimized visible-light diethylamine conditions, what hydrogen-production rate is observed for the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer, and what structural or electronic features are associated with its activity?

How does the choice of sacrificial electron donor affect hydrogen production by the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer under the reported visible-light conditions?

What transient photocurrent and chronoamperometric measurements indicate about charge generation and separation in the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer under visible-light irradiation?

What photoluminescence intensity and time-resolved decay indicate about photogenerated carrier recombination in the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer?

Do control experiments under similar photocatalytic conditions support water as the hydrogen source for the manganese-containing fluorescein 2,2'-bipyridine coordination polymer system?

What crystal structure and chemical formula define Co4-Co-MOF, and how are its cobalt sulfate clusters connected within the framework?

What coordination and sulfate-connectivity pattern makes the Co4(SO4)4 cluster in Co4-Co-MOF a distorted cube-like unit?

What Co-O, Co-N, and Co···Co distances characterize the Co4(SO4)4 cluster in Co4-Co-MOF?

What powder X-ray diffraction evidence supports the identity and phase purity of bulk Co4-Co-MOF?

What X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy signals support the presence of Co(II) ions and the assigned bonding environments in Co4-Co-MOF?
